merger_description:
INNIO Holding GmbH (INNIO Holding), through its wholly owned subsidiaries INNIO Jenbacher International B.V. (INNIO Jenbacher International) and INNIO Jenbacher Netherlands B.V. (INNIO Jenbacher Netherlands) (together with their affiliates, the **INNIO Group**) proposes to acquire 100% of the share capital in Enerflex Service Pty Limited (**Enerflex**). The Target Companies provide aftermarket services (spare parts, repair and maintenance) for gas compression and energy infrastructure. (the **Acquisition**).

INNIO Group is a global manufacturer of gas power units under the Jenbacher and Waukesha brands.

INNIO Group manufactures gas power units and genuine spare parts at its facilities (primarily in Austria for Jenbacher and the United States, and Canada for Waukesha) and supplies these globally through distributors, including in Australia.

Enerflex Australia is an aftermarket services provider for energy infrastructure operators in Australia. It provides maintenance, repair, replacement of spare parts, field services, retrofits, and the supply of gas power units (new and refurbished as replacements) as part of their aftermarket services for a wide variety of gas compression and power generation units and other related equipment, such as compressor units and electric motors.

determination_table_content.details:
INNIO Group’s (INNIO) proposed acquisition of 100% of the share
capital in Enerflex Service Pty Limited (Enerflex Service), which
provides aftermarket services (spare parts, repair and maintenance)
for gas compression and energy infrastructure (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

INNIO Holding GmbH (INNIO Holding), through its wholly owned
subsidiaries INNIO Jenbacher International B.V. and INNIO
Jenbacher Netherlands B.V. (together with their affiliates, the INNIO
Group) proposes to acquire 100% of the share capital in Enerflex
Service Pty Limited (Enerflex Service).
INNIO Group is a global manufacturer of gas power units under the
Jenbacher and Waukesha brands.
INNIO Group manufactures gas power units and genuine spare parts
at its facilities (primarily in Austria for Jenbacher, and the United
States and Canada for Waukesha) and supplies these globally
through distributors, including in Australia.
The target, Enerflex Service is an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of
Enerflex Ltd (together with all its subsidiaries, Enerflex Group).
Enerflex Service is an aftermarket services provider for energy
infrastructure operators in Australia. It provides maintenance, repair,
replacement of spare parts, field services, retrofits, and the supply of
gas power units (new and refurbished as replacements) as part of
their aftermarket services for a wide variety of gas compression and
power generation units and other related equipment, such as
compressor units and electric motors.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the parties
determination_table_content.details:
The parties have a vertical relationship. Enerflex Service supplies
aftermarket services for Waukesha gas power units to owners and
operators of such units, and sources Waukesha spare parts and gas
power units from INNIO for owners and operators of such units.
INNIO does not provide aftermarket services and has no direct sales
of Waukesha spare parts or power units to Australia, and Enerflex
Australia does not manufacture power units.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form information from third partes, including
submissions expressing concerns that the Acquisition would lead to
reduced competitive tension in the supply of Waukesha spare parts
and/or foreclosure of rival aftermarket service suppliers who rely on
access to Waukesha spare parts.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings:
• There is no horizontal overlap between INNIO and Enerflex
Service. INNIO does not provide aftermarket services and
has no direct sales of Waukesha spare parts or power units
to Australia and Enerflex Service does not manufacture
power units.
• There are a number of other OEM gas unit suppliers and
aftermarket service suppliers in Australia that compete in
the supply of gas compression power units and aftermarket
services for gas compression power units respectively.
• INNIO is unlikely to have requisite market power in
downstream aftermarket services markets or upstream OEM
gas unit markets to have the ability to foreclose its upstream
or downstream competitors by raising prices or reducing
service with respect to the supply of Waukesha spare parts
or aftermarket services to competitors.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
